Recommended implementation, synthesized from SASRec masking and PyTorch numerical guidance: use `valid = sequence.ne(0)` and process occurrences by sequence position; repeated IDs remain separate events. In FP32, maintain `S = a*S + valid*x` and `Z = a*Z + valid`, returning `S/Z.clamp_min(eps)` and explicitly zeroing padded outputs. Initialize both states to zero. For interaction-distance decay, use constant `a = exp(-softplus(theta))` per valid interaction; skip state updates on padding. For timestamp decay, use `a = exp(-lambda*delta_time)` between consecutive valid events, with explicit time units and nonnegative gaps. Avoid cumulative positive exponentials followed by cancellation, which can overflow. SASRec’s causal attention mask must also remain intact. [SASRec implementation](https://github.com/pmixer/SASRec.pytorch/blob/main/python/model.py), [PyTorch numerical guidance](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/main/notes/numerical_accuracy.html).

Normalize pooled and SASRec branches separately over the feature dimension before fusion, then remask padding: affine normalization can otherwise reintroduce nonzero padding. A practical fusion is `LN(h) + tanh(g)*LN(pool)`, initializing `g` around `1e-3`; this preserves baseline scale while allowing immediate branch gradients. This near-zero choice is an engineering adaptation of zero-initialized residual gating, rather than a proven optimum. [LayerNorm](https://docs.pytorch.org/docs/stable/generated/torch.nn.LayerNorm.html), [ReZero](https://proceedings.mlr.press/v161/bachlechner21a.html).

Numerical checks: compare every prefix against an explicit float64 weighted-sum reference; alter suffix tokens and verify earlier outputs remain unchanged; check zero gradients from earlier outputs to future inputs. Include repeated items, all-padding rows, single events, equal timestamps, extreme gaps, and decay approaching zero or one. With dropout disabled, compare batched training-path features against prediction-path features for identical prefixes, padding, positions, and truncation; verify checkpoint reload parity, finite gradients, and tolerance-based agreement rather than bitwise equality.
